claims.statement: For finite disjoint positive-size blocks of total size M, H=product_i((1+z)^{s_i}+z) satisfies H[k]/binom(M,k)=average over k-subsets S of product_i(1+X_i(S)/s_i), where X_i marks singleton occupancy. Finite AM-GM, log(1+1/s)>=2/(2s+1), and the nonnegative Taylor remainder imply H[k]>=binom(M,k) E_d(y_k) for 0<=k<=M and every d>=0, with y_k=sum_i (2s_i/(2s_i+1))*binom(M-s_i,k-1)/binom(M,k). Zero extension followed by nonnegative convolution with GF_r gives a coefficient lower bound for path-star T_i, using GF_2=(1,2), GF_3=(2,5,2), GF_4=(3,9,7,2).
claims.scope: Universal finite-block coefficient statement for 0<=k<=M; zero-extended coefficient bound and path-star cofactor convolution at natural j. Empty block family is permitted. It implies no selector, descent, MASS, exact-ratio payment, or aggregate statement. Informal proof only in this worker report.
claims.reason: The finite-set expansion and singleton-event count prove the identity directly without independence. Applying finite AM-GM to the positive rational subset weights gives the exact integer-power inequality; the derivative proof of the logarithm bound and the nonnegative Taylor remainder close the coefficient chain. Exact small-profile replay is supporting bounded evidence only.
